title: Several digital-asset treasury firms have pivoted to AI amid a slump in crypto prices, but their poor stock performance suggests the strategy is not working (Monique Mulima/Bloomberg)
blurb: Several digital-asset treasury firms have pivoted to AI ventures as the crypto price slump erodes the mark-to-market value of their token holdings. Their sagging stock prices suggest the shift isn't convincing investors, leaving these companies stuck between a weak core treasury and an unproven AI strategy.

title: How onchain analysts demix Tornado Cash transactions
blurb: This walkthrough breaks down how onchain analysts de-anonymize Tornado Cash withdrawals, using deposit-and-withdrawal timing correlation, reused relayers, gas-funding trails, and address-clustering heuristics to link mixed funds back to their source. The author illustrates each technique with real transaction traces, showing how the mixer's anonymity set collapses when users batch deposits, reuse wallets, or withdraw to previously linked addresses.

title: Melee Launches Parimutuel Market Maker for Solana Prediction Markets
blurb: Melee launched a parimutuel market maker for prediction markets on Solana, pooling all stakes on an outcome and paying winners proportionally from the losing side rather than quoting prices through an order book or constant-product curve. The design removes the need for dedicated liquidity providers, letting low-volume or long-tail markets settle without the thin books and slippage that typically plague on-chain prediction venues.

title: TD Cowen cuts David Bailey’s Nakamoto target 58% after bitcoin outlook reset
blurb: TD Cowen cut its price target on David Bailey-led Nakamoto by 58%, citing pressure on the bitcoin treasury company's capital structure from BTC's recent decline. The revision reflects how leveraged bitcoin-accumulation vehicles reprice faster than the underlying asset when treasury values fall relative to the debt and equity raised to fund purchases.

title: Morpho Midnight Analysis
blurb: Morpho launched Midnight, a fixed-term loan product that prices loans like bonds: lenders buy a credit unit at a discount that redeems at par at maturity, locking the rate rather than letting it reprice each block. The design targets institutional loan books already on Morpho, including Coinbase's $1.4B+ cbBTC-backed facility. Terms across 1, 3, and 6 months form a yield curve, though offer-based liquidity remains unproven at scale.

title: Phantom to End Monad Support on Aug. 26
blurb: Phantom will end support for the Monad network on Aug. 26, cutting off the high-throughput EVM chain roughly nine months after its November 2025 mainnet launch as the wallet refocuses on its core business and the Robinhood Chain. The exit exposes a distribution gap for Monad, whose MON token trades at $0.0205, down 58% from its all-time high, though rivals MetaMask, Backpack, and Rabby moved to absorb the users.

title: Crypto stocks rally thanks to rotation from AI infrastructure; bitcoin miners lag
blurb: Crypto stocks led Monday's market as capital rotated out of chip and AI infrastructure names, with Strategy up 7%, Coinbase and BitGo gaining 4% to 6%, and ether accumulator Bitmine Immersion surging 11% after adding nearly 10,000 ETH. AI-exposed bitcoin miners lagged, with Cipher Mining down 8% and pure-play names Riot and CleanSpark falling 5% and 4% as investors reprice them as AI infrastructure.

title: Crypto’s favorite $90 trillion trading product is coming to Wall Street, but big banks are taking it slow
blurb: Perpetual futures, the non-expiring contracts that Bank of America estimates at roughly $90 trillion in annual volume, are entering regulated US markets after the CFTC cleared Kalshi and Coinbase to list them. Prop shops, market makers, and newer clearing firms are moving first, while large banks study the products but hold off on major launches over capital, compliance, and clearing costs.

title: Ant International raises $1.2B for global expansion
blurb: Ant International raised $1.2B to fund global expansion, deepening its push into cross-border payments, treasury management, and merchant acquiring outside China. The round positions the Ant Group affiliate to compete more directly with Stripe, Adyen, and Wise on international settlement rails, particularly across Southeast Asia and emerging markets where it already processes large wallet-to-wallet volumes.

title: South Korea’s KB Kookmin Bank to launch cross-border payment service on JPMorgan’s Kinexys: report
blurb: KB Kookmin Bank, South Korea's largest bank, will launch a blockchain-based cross-border corporate payments service next month on JPMorgan's Kinexys network, becoming the first Korean institution to settle import and export transactions on the rail. The service starts with US dollar transfers across 10 countries through the bank's domestic and Singapore branches, extending Kinexys' near-real-time institutional settlement into Korean trade finance.

title: EDX Markets Closes $76M Series C Led by SBI Holdings
blurb: EDX Markets, an institution-only crypto trading venue with its own central clearinghouse, closed a $76M Series C led by SBI Holdings, making the Tokyo-listed financial group a strategic investor in the US exchange. The raise funds expansion of EDX's clearing and settlement capabilities and follows its OCC application to charter EDX Trust, a proposed national trust bank for regulated custody and settlement.

title: Nubank to acquire Banco Porto Real de Investimentos, strengthen Brazil operation
blurb: Nubank agreed to acquire Banco Porto Real de Investimentos, a Rio de Janeiro wholesale-credit bank, adding its banking license to Nubank's existing Brazilian licenses pending Central Bank approval. The new license carries no additional capital or liquidity requirements and leaves service unchanged for Nubank's 115 million customers, deepening its position as Brazil's largest private financial institution by customer count.

title: A federal judge issues a preliminary injunction blocking Minnesota from enforcing a newly enacted law that banned prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket (Nate Raymond/Reuters)
blurb: A federal judge granted a preliminary injunction barring Minnesota from enforcing its new law banning prediction markets, allowing Kalshi and Polymarket to keep operating in the state while the case proceeds. The ruling adds to a growing body of court decisions favoring the CFTC-regulated event-contract platforms over state gambling regulators, strengthening their argument that federal commodities oversight preempts state-level bans.

title: Kalshi, Polymarket win pause against Minnesota's prediction market ban
blurb: A federal judge granted Kalshi, Polymarket, and the CFTC a preliminary injunction against Minnesota's law criminalizing prediction markets, ruling the state statute is likely preempted by the federal Commodity Exchange Act. The decision reinforces the CFTC's jurisdiction over event contracts structured as swaps, undercutting state-level efforts to ban prediction markets while the case proceeds to a full trial.

title: Inside the CME and CFTC’s battle over onchain perpetual futures
blurb: CME Group sued the CFTC and chairman Mike Selig over the agency's decision to let Coinbase and Kalshi list onchain perpetual futures, leveraged crypto contracts with no expiration date. A federal court ruling will shape how the US regulates perps, a market that reached a reported $60T in offshore volume last year and threatens CME's long-dated futures franchise.

title: Chime launches in-app investing
blurb: Chime launched Chime Invest, letting users trade stocks and ETFs commission-free or hold an Atomic Invest-managed portfolio with no account minimums and management fees ranging from 0% to 0.25% by membership tier. The move deepens Chime's push to rebundle banking, investing, and lending in one app, keeping the roughly 50 monthly transactions per member inside its ecosystem rather than a third-party brokerage.

title: X Money is launching in the US starting today
blurb: X launched X Money in the US, a digital wallet with Venmo-style peer-to-peer payments, Apple Wallet support, and a metal Visa card users can brand with their handle. The rollout is limited to Premium and Premium Plus subscribers, advertises up to 6% APY for paying tiers, and follows earlier scrutiny from Senator Elizabeth Warren over consumer and financial-stability risks.

title: Payments M&A spools up
blurb: Payments M&A activity is accelerating in 2026, with strategic acquirers and private-equity buyers moving on processors, gateways, and infrastructure providers after a multi-year lull in dealmaking. The pickup reflects steadier interest rates and pressure on subscale payments firms to consolidate, setting up more roll-ups as larger platforms buy distribution and rail coverage rather than build it.

title: Amazon Business adds Affirm as its first BNPL option at checkout
blurb: Amazon Business added Affirm as its first buy-now-pay-later option at checkout, marking the launch of Affirm's new B2B pay-over-time product for sole proprietors. Eligible customers get an instant credit decision and can split eligible purchases across three to 48 months with no late or hidden fees, rolling out now and reaching all eligible sole proprietors by Black Friday.

title: Judge blocks Minnesota from enforcing prediction market ban in win for Kalshi, Polymarket
blurb: A federal judge granted a preliminary injunction blocking Minnesota from enforcing its new law banning prediction markets, letting Kalshi and Polymarket keep operating in the state while the CFTC-backed suit proceeds. The court found the statute is likely preempted by the Commodity Exchange Act, reinforcing the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction over event contracts even as Kalshi lost parallel bids to block New York and Michigan enforcement.

title: X rolls out X Money to US Premium and Premium+ subscribers, combining a deposit account with up to 6% APY, free instant transfers on X, and a Visa debit card (Zac Hall/9to5Mac)
blurb: X launched X Money for US Premium and Premium+ subscribers, pairing a deposit account paying up to 6% APY with a Visa debit card and free instant peer-to-peer transfers inside the app. The rollout leans on a bank partner for deposits and marks X's first consumer banking product, positioning the platform to compete with Cash App and PayPal on everyday payments.

title: Profitable Serbian-Hungarian InsurTech Ominimo hits unicorn status two years after launch
blurb: Ominimo, a profitable Serbian-Hungarian motor-insurance startup, raised €20.1M at a €1.4B valuation from the EBRD's venture arm, reaching unicorn status two years after its 2024 launch. The company's data-driven pricing pushed its annualized gross written premium run-rate from €26.3M in 2024 to roughly €306.8M today, and it plans to secure its own insurance licence and enter the US in 2027.

title: X Money is finally here, and it’s much more than a digital wallet
blurb: X began rolling out X Money to Premium and Premium+ subscribers in the US, adding in-app peer-to-peer transfers, a deposit account with up to 6% APY and FDIC insurance via a partner-bank sweep, and an X Visa debit card with 3% cashback. The launch pushes Musk's everything-app ambition directly against Venmo, Cash App, and PayPal, with expansion gated on state-by-state regulatory approvals.

title: Marqeta partners with Zerohash for stablecoin-linked cards
blurb: Marqeta partnered with Zerohash to let any of its customers embed stablecoin-linked cards into new or existing card programs without rebuilding core systems or taking on new regulatory burden. The move gives Marqeta's thousands of live programs a switch-on path to stablecoin spend, but its US model requires a sponsor bank that takes an interchange cut, unlike Puerto Rico-based rival Rain, which issues directly as a Visa principal member.

title: Intuit launches business credit card that syncs natively with QuickBooks
blurb: Intuit launched a business credit card that syncs transactions natively with QuickBooks, auto-categorizing spend and reconciling against the books in real time rather than through periodic feed imports. The card leans on Intuit's underwriting via QuickBooks financial data, targeting small businesses already inside the accounting platform and tightening its grip on the SMB money-movement stack.

title: Big banks' record Wall Street profits are increasingly tied to AI
blurb: The five largest Wall Street banks reported $114B in capital markets revenue for the first half of 2026, up 31.5% year-over-year, with stock trading tied to the AI boom driving more than half the gain. AI is fueling underwriting fees, equities trading, and wealth inflows from IPO employees, though executives including Jamie Dimon warned the trading haul is "close to as good as it gets.

title: Ramp launches AI token spend controls
blurb: Ramp launched AI Token Spend Management, a dashboard that lets finance teams track and cap AI token and subscription spend across Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, and Gemini in one place. The tool ties usage to cost, flags savings and anomalies, and sets limits by team, project, or API key, addressing a category that has grown 20.7x across Ramp customers since June 2025.

title: Augustus secures $180 million Series B
blurb: Augustus raised $180M in a Series B at a $1B valuation, led by Tiger Global with the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Circle, and Deel participating, to build a federally chartered bank giving international fintechs and banks direct access to USD accounts and payment rails. By pursuing a charter rather than renting one, Augustus is positioning to disintermediate the sponsor-bank layer that firms outside the US currently depend on for dollar clearing.

title: Paschi, BPM Advisers Working on Merger to Foil Intesa’s Bid
blurb: Advisers for Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena and Banco BPM are in talks over a possible cash-and-stock merger that would effectively block Intesa Sanpaolo's €35B ($40B) takeover bid for Monte Paschi. A Paschi-BPM tie-up would reshape Italy's consolidation race, creating a third domestic banking pole large enough to defend against Intesa while complicating Rome's plans to fully exit its remaining Monte Paschi stake.

title: NFL urges CFTC to strengthen rules on sports prediction markets: report
blurb: The NFL sent a letter to CFTC Chair Michael Selig urging stricter rules on sports prediction markets, arguing the agency's proposed event-contract rulemaking falls short on protecting game integrity and consumers and should add age and advertising restrictions. The push splits the league from the NHL and MLB, which have partnered with Kalshi and Polymarket, and tests how far Selig's pro-innovation CFTC will regulate contracts tied to live games.

title: Samsung launches Galaxy Card seven years after Apple Card
blurb: Samsung launched the Galaxy Card, a virtual-first credit card issued by Barclays on the Visa network, offering up to 5% cash back and managed inside Samsung Wallet, seven years after Apple Card debuted. The card mirrors Apple's model with tiered rewards, but Samsung's narrow services footprint means the headline 5% rate applies mostly to Samsung hardware purchases rather than everyday spending.

title: X Money begins limited US rollout
blurb: X began a limited US rollout of X Money, its in-app payments and banking service built on a Visa Direct integration, initially restricted to Premium and Premium X subscribers. The gated launch lets X test peer-to-peer transfers and account funding with a small user base before a wider release, extending its bid to turn the platform into an everything app.

title: Decathlon Germany adds Wero payment option to decathlon.de website
blurb: Decathlon Germany switched on Wero, the European Payments Initiative's account-to-account rail, at decathlon.de on July 20, making Germany the first market in the retailer's footprint to carry the scheme. Wero routes real-time payments directly between bank accounts with in-app biometric authorization, letting Decathlon bypass the 1-2% card interchange paid to Visa and Mastercard while tying the option to its membership program.

title: Crypto’s favorite $90 trillion trading product is coming to Wall Street, but big banks are taking it slow
blurb: Perpetual futures, the non-expiring contracts that Bank of America pegs at roughly $90 trillion in annual crypto volume, are moving onshore after the CFTC cleared Kalshi and Coinbase to list them, with Kalshi topping $1B in volume within a week of its June launch. Prop shops, market makers, and newer clearing firms will lead adoption while big banks, bound by stricter capital rules and reputational risk, study the products before committing.

title: Hong Kong’s central bank puts a number on lenders' quantum preparedness. It's very low.
blurb: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority published its first Quantum Preparedness Index, scoring the territory's banking sector just 2.3 out of 10 on readiness for post-quantum cryptography. Most banks remain stuck in the awareness phase with no formal migration plans, leaving them exposed to "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks as the HKMA pushes the industry toward a 10 by 2030.
